title: Jio Financial Services Q1 Profit Surges 156% to Rs 830 Crore as Lending Engine Hits Rs 30,000 Crore
excerpt: Mukesh Ambani's financial arm crosses the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark for the first time, with assets under management nearly tripling year-on-year to Rs 30,667 crore.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jio Financial Services' Q1 profit surged 156% to Rs 830 crore, driven by lending growth.
  • Revenue nearly tripled to Rs 2,005 crore, marking a significant milestone for the company.
  • Assets under management increased 2.6 times to Rs 30,667 crore, reflecting strong lending performance.
  • Payments vertical showed growth, with total payment value rising 2.5 times to Rs 19,208 crore.
  • Total expenses increased 291% to Rs 991 crore, impacting profit margins amid rapid expansion.

> **"Total payment value grew 2.5 times to Rs 19,208 crore."** ![Mukesh Ambani — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/69/Mukesh_Ambani.jpg)
  • Jio Financial Services reported consolidated net profit of Rs 830 crore in Q1 FY27, a 156 percent jump from Rs 325 crore a year ago.
  • Revenue from operations nearly tripled to Rs 2,005 crore from Rs 619 crore, crossing the Rs 2,000 crore mark for the first time.
  • The lending arm's assets under management surged 2.6 times to Rs 30,667 crore, while the JioBlackRock asset management venture grew AUM to Rs 18,412 crore.
  • Motilal Oswal retained a buy rating with a target price of Rs 315, though it trimmed EPS estimates by 4-6 percent on elevated operating expenses.

Jio Financial Services posted its strongest quarter since listing, with consolidated net profit more than doubling to Rs 830 crore in the three months ending June 2026 — driven by an aggressive ramp-up in its lending business and the first meaningful contributions from its payments and asset management arms.

The results mark a turning point for Mukesh Ambani's financial services bet. Carved out from Reliance Industries in 2023, Jio Financial has spent the past three years building a full-stack financial ecosystem. The June quarter suggests that ecosystem is finally generating operating leverage at scale.

The Lending Engine

The NBFC arm was the primary growth driver. Assets under management surged 2.6 times year-on-year to Rs 30,667 crore from Rs 11,665 crore, while disbursements jumped 173 percent. Net interest income came in at Rs 257 crore, and the lending vertical posted a standalone profit of Rs 96 crore.

Interest income soared 165 percent year-on-year to Rs 962 crore, while fees and commission income rose 506 percent to Rs 325 crore. The capital adequacy ratio stood at a comfortable 22.35 percent, with the average borrowing cost at 7.07 percent — giving the company headroom for further balance sheet expansion.

Payments Turn the Corner

The payments vertical showed signs of operational maturity. Total payment value grew 2.5 times to Rs 19,208 crore. Gross fee and commission income jumped 6.4 times to Rs 176 crore, while net fee and commission income rose 3.4 times to Rs 24 crore as operating leverage improved.

Jio Payments Bank continued its turnaround, with total income surging 7.7 times to Rs 83 crore. Customer deposits increased 72 percent to Rs 617 crore, and the customer base grew 51 percent to 3.9 million. The bank also launched FASTag ANPR-based multi-lane free flow toll processing at 19 toll plazas.

The company additionally launched cross-border collection services during the quarter, enabling Indian exporters to accept international payments — a potentially significant play for small businesses in the diaspora ecosystem.

"The sustained business momentum across our verticals validates the granular architecture of our full-stack ecosystem and the strength of our execution."

— Hitesh Sethia, Managing Director and CEO, Jio Financial Services

Asset Management and Insurance

JioBlackRock Asset Management saw closing AUM rise 21 percent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 18,412 crore. The venture expanded its product suite with the Prism Specialised Investment Fund and received regulatory approval to set up a retail fund management entity in GIFT City.

Jio Insurance Broking facilitated premiums worth Rs 238 crore, up 55 percent year-on-year. The Allianz Jio Reinsurance joint venture underwrote gross written premiums of Rs 266 crore in its first full quarter of operations. During the quarter, the company also incorporated Jio Allianz General Insurance as a 50:50 joint venture with Allianz.

The Cost Question

The rapid growth came with a price tag. Total expenses ballooned 291 percent to Rs 991 crore, driven by rising finance costs and staff expenses required to build out the super-app infrastructure. Pre-provisioning operating profit before dividend income rose a more modest 38 percent to Rs 505 crore.

Motilal Oswal trimmed its FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates by 4 percent and 6 percent respectively, citing elevated operating expenses. But the brokerage retained its buy rating with a target price of Rs 315, noting that its valuation does not yet factor in contributions from insurance manufacturing, wealth management, broking, and marketplace businesses — all still in incubation.

What to Watch

Shares of Jio Financial Services climbed over 3 percent on July 17, closing at Rs 242.98 on the NSE, after hitting an intraday high of Rs 249.95. The stock's trajectory will depend on whether the company can sustain its current AUM growth trajectory while bringing operating expenses under control as new business lines mature. For NRI investors tracking Reliance's financial ambitions, the JioBlackRock GIFT City entity and cross-border payments launch are particularly worth monitoring.
